routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: EU and Nordic citizens need no visa. Citizens of visa-free countries can visit with a valid passport. Stays are up to 90 days and the Schengen 90 in 180 days rule applies. The official visa-free list was not readable, so check the Ministry for Foreign Affairs list.

other: Official visa-free country list not confirmed. ETIAS and the 90/180 rule were not on the page read.

routes.name: Short-stay Schengen visa (type C)
routes.summary: Most people from countries that are not visa-free need a visa for visits up to 90 days. Apply at a Finnish embassy abroad, which also decides on it.

other: Visa fee and validity not confirmed. The Ministry for Foreign Affairs site has them.

routes.name: Seasonal work visa or permit
routes.summary: Seasonal work can last up to nine months in any 12-month period. Under 3 months you need a seasonal work visa or a certificate. From 3 to 9 months you need a residence permit for seasonal work. Family members can't get permits based on a seasonal worker.

other: For 6 to 9 months a labour market test applies.
You can't start work before the permit is granted.

stay.note: Max nine months in any 12-month period

routes.name: Residence permit for an employed person
routes.summary: For people who work under an employer's direction. Details such as pay thresholds were not readable, so check Migri before applying.

other: Fees and pay requirements not confirmed.

routes.name: Residence permit for a specialist
routes.summary: A work-based permit category for specialists. Details were not readable on the page read, so check Migri.

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: For degree holders with a job of at least one year. You need a contract or binding job offer stating duties and salary. A Finnish Blue Card is issued for up to two years at a time.

eligibility.education: Higher education degree, at least 3 years of study after upper secondary
other: Salary threshold not stated on the page read.

routes.name: Residence permit for a self-employed person
routes.summary: For entrepreneurs, freelancers and light entrepreneurs. Your income must come from your business. Finland has no separate digital nomad visa that was found on Migri.

other: Funds, fees and duration not confirmed.

routes.name: Start-up entrepreneur residence permit
routes.summary: You need a positive eligibility statement from Business Finland first. A first permit can be granted for 2 years. You must show enough funds for the whole permit period. Fast track can take about two weeks.

other: Positive Business Finland eligibility statement required.
Start-up work must be your main activity.

routes.processing: Fast-track service can take about two weeks, per Migri.

routes.name: Researcher residence permit
routes.summary: For researchers, granted under national law or under an EU directive. Check Migri for details.

routes.name: Student residence permit
routes.summary: Covers the whole length of your studies. Degree students usually get a continuous (A) permit. You must show enough funds. You can work an average of 30 hours a week. Non-EU students may also face tuition fees.

other: Monthly funds amount not stated on the page read.

routes.name: Post-study residence permit for job seeking
routes.summary: Available after completing a degree, to look for work. Duration, fee and conditions were not readable, so check Migri.

other: Not available if you applied for asylum or have an unexecuted deportation decision. Duration and fee not confirmed.

routes.name: Family ties residence permits
routes.summary: Permits exist for spouses and partners, children and other family. The Migri family page could not be read, so income rules and fees are not confirmed.

other: Income requirement, fees and eligible relatives not confirmed.

routes.name: Permanent residence permit
routes.summary: You need 4 years of uninterrupted residence on a continuous (A) permit, with at least 2 of those years lived in Finland. Apply in Finland while your permit is valid, up to 3 months before the 4 years end. The page read gave no income, language or fee details.

other: Apply no earlier than 3 months before finishing 4 years. Applying from abroad is handled as a first permit.

routes.name: Finnish citizenship by naturalization
routes.summary: Since the 1 October 2024 change, the standard residence period is 8 years of legal residence, and you must live in Finland when you apply. It drops to 5 years with the required language skills, marriage or partnership with a Finn (3 years living together), or if stateless. It is 2 years for Nordic citizens. You need satisfactory Finnish, Swedish or sign language, a clear identity, integrity and means of support.

eligibility.language: Satisfactory Finnish, Swedish, Finnish Sign Language or Finland-Swedish Sign Language
other: 3 years in rare cases with permanent full-time work or very serious reasons.
Exact language level, test and fee not stated on the pages read. Applications submitted before 1 October 2024 follow older rules.

citizenship.note: Finland does not make you give up your current citizenship. Your other country may require it.

routes.name: Citizenship with a Finnish spouse or partner
routes.summary: The residence period is 5 years if you are married to or partnered with a Finnish citizen and have lived together at least 3 years. The same language, integrity and means of support rules apply.

other: At least 3 years of living together with the Finnish spouse or partner.

routes.name: Asylum in Finland
routes.summary: You must be in Finland to apply. Apply in person to the border authority, police or the Finnish Immigration Service. Applications by mail, email or at Finnish missions abroad are not accepted.
steps: Apply in person at a border authority, police station or Migri location.
Register the application with police or border authorities.
Lodge it with Migri within 21 days of registering, or 5 days in the border procedure.

routes.name: EU, EEA and Nordic free movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can live and work in Finland. Staying over 3 months means registering your right of residence. Details were only partly confirmed.

other: Registration rules beyond the 3 month point not confirmed on a page read.
